items.title: UnitedHealth vs. Johnson & Johnson: Which Stock Is the Better Buy After Q3 Earnings?
items.summary: UnitedHealth and Johnson & Johnson both raised full-year guidance after Q3 earnings, but with contrasting performance. UnitedHealth beat expectations with 60% YoY EPS growth driven by improved medical cost management, while J&J saw earnings decline 7.5% YoY despite pharmaceutical growth offsetting weak MedTech performance. UnitedHealth is recommended as the better buy due to stronger earnings momentum, lower valuation (19X vs 23X forward earnings), and higher dividend yield (2.45% vs 2%).

items.title: Prediction: Johnson & Johnson Will Be a Faster-Growing Company by 2030 Than Most Investors Expect
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson is positioned for faster growth by 2030 following its separation from its slower-growing consumer health division. The company can now focus investments on its faster-growing biopharma and medtech segments. Key growth drivers include recent drug approvals like ICOTYDE and the FDA-cleared Ottava robotic surgery system, which operates in a market with significant expansion potential. Despite challenges from government price negotiations and talc-related lawsuits, J&J's diversified portfolio and strong dividend history make it an attractive long-term investment.
